question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

28, 57, 115, 231, 463, 927, ? , 3711
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1855.

GIVEN

• 28, 57, 115, 231, 463, 927, ? , 3711

SOLUTION

• The rule is: next term = (previous term × 2) + 1.

• 28×2+1 = 57; 57×2+1 = 115; 115×2+1 = 231; 231×2+1 = 463; 463×2+1 = 927.

• Missing term = 927×2+1 = 1855.

• Check: 1855×2+1 = 3711 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each term is roughly double the previous; multiply by 2 and add 1 — 927×2+1 = 1855.

NOTE

• For fast-growing series, test the pattern aₙ = a₍ₙ₋₁₎×2 ± c or ×3 ± c before checking differences.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

G, D, X, U, O, L, F, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. C.

GIVEN

• G, D, X, U, O, L, F, ?

SOLUTION

• Split into two alternate series.

• Odd positions: G(7), X(24), O(15), F(6) → +17, −9, −9.

• Even positions: D(4), U(21), L(12), ? → +17, −9, −9.

• So ? = L(12) − 9 = 3 = C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Look at every 2nd letter: D→U→L→? drops by 9 (U to L), so L−9 = C.

NOTE

• Use position numbers A=1…Z=26; when a value ≤ 0, add 26 to wrap around.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

ST : UW :: ? : FJ :: QI : SL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. DG.

GIVEN

• ST : UW :: ? : FJ :: QI : SL

SOLUTION

• Relation (1st→2nd): S(19)+2=U, T(20)+3=W → letters shift by +2, +3.

• Check (QI→SL): Q(17)+2=S, I(9)+3=L ✓.

• Apply reverse to FJ: F(6)−2 = D(4); J(10)−3 = G(7).

• So ? = DG.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Second cluster = first shifted (+2,+3). Reverse it on FJ: F−2=D, J−3=G.

NOTE

• In analogy pairs, fix the letter-shift pattern from a complete pair, then apply it forward or backward as needed.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

MJ, KF, IB, ?, ET, CP, AL, YH
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. GX.

GIVEN

• MJ, KF, IB, ?, ET, CP, AL, YH

SOLUTION

• First letters: M(13), K(11), I(9), ?, E(5), C(3), A(1), Y(25) → decrease by 2. Missing = 9−2 = 7 = G.

• Second letters: J(10), F(6), B(2), ?, T(20), P(16), L(12), H(8) → decrease by 4. Missing = 2−4 = −2 → +26 = 24 = X.

• So ? = GX.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each cluster: 1st letter −2, 2nd letter −4. From IB: I−2=G, B−4=X (wrap) = GX.

NOTE

• When subtraction gives ≤0, add 26 to stay in the A–Z range.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

FO : DK :: RY : PU :: QB : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. OX.

GIVEN

• FO : DK :: RY : PU :: QB : ?

SOLUTION

• Relation (1st→2nd cluster): F(6)−2=D, O(15)−4=K → shift −2, −4.

• Check (RY→PU): R(18)−2=P, Y(25)−4=U ✓.

• Apply to QB: Q(17)−2 = O(15); B(2)−4 = −2 → +26 = 24 = X.

• So ? = OX.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same rule as the given pairs: 1st letter −2, 2nd letter −4. Q−2=O, B−4=X.

NOTE

• Always confirm the shift on the second sample pair before applying it to the unknown.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(ND, PF, RH)

(QP, SR, UT)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (KJ, ML, ON).

GIVEN

• (ND, PF, RH) and (QP, SR, UT)

SOLUTION

• Within each set, both letters of successive clusters increase by +2.

• (ND, PF, RH): first letters N,P,R (+2); second letters D,F,H (+2).

• (QP, SR, UT): first Q,S,U (+2); second P,R,T (+2).

• Option (KJ, ML, ON): first K,M,O (+2); second J,L,N (+2) ✓.

• Others fail: e.g. (GN,IM,KQ) second letters N,M,Q are not +2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check if both letters advance by +2 across the three clusters — only KJ, ML, ON does.

NOTE

• For 'odd-set-out', test the simplest common progression (a fixed step in each letter position) first.

question: 5th of a month is Tuesday. This month has 31 days. What will be the 12th of next month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• 5th of a month = Tuesday; month has 31 days.

SOLUTION

• From the 5th of this month to the 5th of next month = 31 days = 31 mod 7 = 3 odd days.

• So 5th of next month = Tuesday + 3 = Friday.

• 12th = 5th + 7 days = same weekday = Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same date next month shifts by (days in month mod 7) = 31 mod 7 = 3 → Tue+3 = Fri; +7 keeps it Friday.

NOTE

• A 31-day month adds 3 odd days, a 30-day month 2, February 0 (28) or 1 (29).

question: A person was born on 27 May 2009. What day of the week will be on his 23rd birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• Date of birth = 27 May 2009; find day on 27 May 2032 (23rd birthday).

SOLUTION

• 27 May 2009 was a Wednesday.

• Over 23 years, odd days = 23 + (number of Feb-29s in the span).

• Leap days between May 2009 and May 2032: 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024, 2028, 2032 = 6.

• Total = 23 + 6 = 29 → 29 mod 7 = 1 odd day.

• So day = Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Net shift = (years + leap-days) mod 7 = 29 mod 7 = 1; Wed + 1 = Thursday.

NOTE

• Each ordinary year adds 1 odd day, each leap year 2; count the Feb-29s that actually fall inside the interval.

question: If 2 January 2400 will be Thursday, then what will be the day on 18 May 2403?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• 2 January 2400 = Thursday.

SOLUTION

• From 2 Jan 2400 to 2 Jan 2403 = 3 years including the 2400 leap day (Feb-29 2400 falls after 2 Jan).

• Odd days = 366 + 365 + 365 = 1096 → 1096 mod 7 = 4. So 2 Jan 2403 = Thursday + 4 = Monday.

• From 2 Jan 2403 to 18 May 2403 = 136 days (Jan 29 + Feb 28 + Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 18) → 136 mod 7 = 3.

• Day = Monday + 3 = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 3-year jump adds 4 odd days (one leap) → Thu→Mon; then 136 days later = +3 → Thursday.

NOTE

• 2400 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year — its Feb-29 counts only if it lies inside the interval.

question: 5 persons P, B, C, G and H are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B is sitting to the immediate left of C. Neither G nor H is the immediate neighbour of C. H is sitting second to the right of P. Who are the immediate neighbours of H?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. B and G.

GIVEN

• 5 persons P, B, C, G, H around a circle, facing centre.

• B is immediate left of C; neither G nor H neighbours C; H is 2nd to the right of P.

SOLUTION

• C's neighbours are B (left) and one more; it can't be G or H, so it is P — C's right neighbour is P.

• Clockwise so far: P, C, B (with B on C's left side).

• H is 2nd to P's right; the remaining two seats take G and H, giving order P, C, B, H, G (clockwise).

• H's immediate neighbours = B and G.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• C is boxed by B and P (only options left), so G and H fill the far side — H lands between B and G.

NOTE

• Facing the centre, a person's immediate left is the clockwise seat and immediate right is anticlockwise.

question: Diameter of 6 circles A, B, C, D, E and F is compared. No two circles have same diameter. Diameter of A is more than only E. Diameter of C is more than F but less than B. Diameter of D is not more than F. If diameter of A is 50, then what will be the possible value of diameter of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 53.

GIVEN

• A > only E ⇒ A is 2nd smallest; C > F, C < B; D < F (D not more than F); A = 50.

SOLUTION

• 'A is more than only E' means A is greater than E and smaller than every other circle: E < A < D, F, C, B.

• Combining C > F > D and A = 50: E < 50 < D < F < C < B.

• So B is the largest and must be greater than 50.

• Among the options, only 53 exceeds 50.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• B is the biggest circle, so B > A = 50; pick the only value above 50 → 53.

NOTE

• 'More than only E' fixes A as the second-smallest — a common phrasing in ranking questions.

question: 7 males A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only four males are to the left of A. B is the immediate neighbour of A and C. D is third to the left of E. F is not the immediate neighbour of E. Who is sitting between D and G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. F.

GIVEN

• Row of 7 facing north; only four males left of A; B neighbours both A and C; D is 3rd to left of E; F not adjacent to E.

SOLUTION

• 'Four to the left of A' ⇒ A is at position 5 (positions 1–7 from left).

• B is between A and C ⇒ C-B-A or A-B-C. Taking A(5), B(6), C(7).

• D is 3rd to left of E ⇒ E at 4, D at 1. Remaining seats 2, 3 for F, G.

• F not adjacent to E(4) means F ≠ 3, so F = 2, G = 3.

• Final: D(1) F(2) G(3) E(4) A(5) B(6) C(7). Between D and G sits F.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix A at seat 5, chain A-B-C to the right, then D & E three apart on the left — F slots between D and G.

NOTE

• Facing north, left = lower position number; '4 to the left' places the person at seat 5.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

QV105 : RS385 :: ? : IT700 :: BT505 : CQ785
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HW420.

GIVEN

• QV105 : RS385 :: ? : IT700 :: BT505 : CQ785

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): Q(17)+1=R, V(22)−3=S, 105+280=385.

• Check (BT505→CQ785): B(2)+1=C, T(20)−3=Q, 505+280=785 ✓.

• Reverse the rule on IT700: I(9)−1=H(8), T(20)+3=W(23), 700−280=420.

• So ? = HW420.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair rule: 1st letter +1, 2nd letter −3, number +280. Undo it on IT700 → HW420.

NOTE

• Keep the number whole (as instructed); find the constant added/subtracted, here +280.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

KIH13 : GED169 :: ? : FSU196 :: RTX17 : NPT289
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JWY14.

GIVEN

• KIH13 : GED169 :: ? : FSU196 :: RTX17 : NPT289

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): each letter −4, number → number².

• KIH → GED: K−4=G, I−4=E, H−4=D; 13² = 169 ✓. Check RTX17→NPT289: R−4=N, T−4=P, X−4=T; 17²=289 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

• Rule: letters −4, number squared. Undo → letters +4, take square root: FSU196 → JWY14.

NOTE

• Recognising a perfect square (169, 289, 196) instantly reveals a square/root relationship.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second number in the same way as the third number is related to the fourth number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : 820 :: 7957 : 8007 :: 5442 : 5492
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 770.

GIVEN

• ? : 820 :: 7957 : 8007 :: 5442 : 5492

SOLUTION

• Relation: second number = first + 50.

• 7957 + 50 = 8007 ✓; 5442 + 50 = 5492 ✓.

• So ? + 50 = 820 ⇒ ? = 820 − 50 = 770.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Every pair differs by +50, so first = 820 − 50 = 770.

NOTE

• Treat numbers as wholes (per instruction); look for a common constant difference across pairs.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

34 : 569 :: 859 : 1394 :: ? : 860
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 325.

GIVEN

• 34 : 569 :: 859 : 1394 :: ? : 860

SOLUTION

• Relation: second number = first + 535.

• 34 + 535 = 569 ✓; 859 + 535 = 1394 ✓.

question: In a certain code language, 'CHIEF' is coded as '28' and 'COURT' is coded as '74'. How will 'REPLY' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 73.

GIVEN

• CHIEF = 28, COURT = 74.

SOLUTION

• Rule: (sum of letter positions) − 3.

• CHIEF = 3+8+9+5+6 = 31; 31 − 3 = 28 ✓.

• COURT = 3+15+21+18+20 = 77; 77 − 3 = 74 ✓.

• REPLY = 18+5+16+12+25 = 76; 76 − 3 = 73.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add positional values (A=1…Z=26) and subtract 3: REPLY sum = 76 → 73.

NOTE

• For number-coding of words, test 'letter-sum ± constant' before multiplying or other rules.

question: In a certain coded language 'MOTEL' is coded as 'OTSAG' and 'FANGS' is coded as 'HFMCN'. How will 'VISIT' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. XNREO.

GIVEN

• MOTEL → OTSAG; FANGS → HFMCN.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts: +2, +5, −1, −4, −5.

• MOTEL: M+2=O, O+5=T, T−1=S, E−4=A, L−5=G ✓. FANGS: F+2=H, A+5=F, N−1=M, G−4=C, S−5=N ✓.

• VISIT: V+2=X, I+5=N, S−1=R, I−4=E, T−5=O.

• So code = XNREO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the fixed shift pattern (+2, +5, −1, −4, −5) to V-I-S-I-T → XNREO.

NOTE

• When a code isn't a uniform shift, check for a per-position shift sequence using both examples.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

AB2, CF116, EJ230, GN344, JS459, KV572
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JS459.

GIVEN

• AB2, CF116, EJ230, GN344, JS459, KV572

SOLUTION

• First letters: A, C, E, G, ?, K → +2 each ⇒ 5th should be I(9), not J.

• Second letters: B, F, J, N, ?, V → +4 each ⇒ 5th should be R(18), not S.

• Numbers: 2, 116, 230, 344, ?, 572 → +114 each ⇒ 5th should be 458, not 459.

• The 5th term should be IR458, so JS459 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step +2/+4 and numbers +114; the 5th term breaks all three ⇒ JS459 is the odd one.

NOTE

• In 'wrong-term' series, verify each attribute (both letters and the number) separately.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

MAL1300, KDH1114, IGD928, GJZ742, FLW556, CPR370
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. FLW556.

GIVEN

• MAL1300, KDH1114, IGD928, GJZ742, FLW556, CPR370

SOLUTION

• First letters: M, K, I, G, ?, C → −2 each ⇒ 5th should be E(5), not F.

• Second letters: A, D, G, J, ?, P → +3 each ⇒ 5th should be M(13), not L.

• Third letters: L, H, D, Z, ?, R → −4 each ⇒ 5th should be V(22), not W.

• Numbers: 1300, 1114, 928, 742, 556, 370 → −186 each (556 is correct).

• Correct 5th term is EMV556, so FLW556 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step −2/+3/−4 and numbers −186; only the letters of the 5th term break ⇒ FLW556.

NOTE

• A term can be wrong in its letters while its number is still correct — check every component.
